confirmed_findings.rule: Relevance and sediment [craft] (Pruning and drift) — a line loses relevance by going stale as the document changes; the cure is a pruning discipline, not letting sediment pile up.

confirmed_findings.rule: Demand [craft] (Steps, completion, and demand) — "watch for criteria that mix checkable and uncheckable terms — one stray uncheckable qualifier inside an otherwise precise list lets the agent satisfy the whole thing impressionistically."
confirmed_findings.target_quote: Polish 4–5 rounds against the same standard as the plan itself — preserve every feature and the plan's full level of detail in each pass.
confirmed_findings.issue: "preserve every feature" is checkable (diffable against the plan's feature list), but "the plan's full level of detail" is a judgment call with no way to tell done from not-done, letting the whole polish bound be satisfied impressionistically.
confirmed_findings.proposed_fix: Replace "the plan's full level of detail" with a checkable proxy, e.g. "the same section count and per-issue field list (migration mechanics, proof-gate dependency, docs dependency) as the plan."
confirmed_findings.reason: panel 3/3 confirmed | CONFIRMED — the quote appears verbatim in the GitHub Issues Handoff section, and the critique is accurate: "preserve every feature" is diffable/checkable, but "the plan's full level of detail" has no operational definition, letting the polish criterion be satisfied impressionistically. || CONFIRMED — the quote appears verbatim in the "GitHub Issues Handoff (Phase 9)" section, and the critique is valid: "preserve every feature" is a checkable criterion while "the plan's full level of detail" is a vague, judgment-based qualifier that undermines objective verification of the polish requirement. || CONFIRMED — the quote appears verbatim in the GitHub Issues Handoff section, and "the plan's full level of detail" is indeed an unfalsifiable qualifier sitting alongside the checkable "preserve every feature," matching the stated rule.

refuted_findings.rule: Duplication [craft] (Pruning and drift) — "an anti-pattern list that restates, negated, rules the document already gives positively is the same meaning written twice — audit such lists against the rules they mirror."
refuted_findings.target_quote: | Extract + rename + reformat in one commit | Kills `git blame` and reviewability; one mechanical move per commit |
refuted_findings.issue: This anti-pattern row (and several neighbors, e.g. "Split along visual sections" vs. the One Rule's "never aesthetically," and "Drop a re-export..." vs. the façade requirement) is the negated restatement of a rule the document already states positively — "one mechanical move per commit" appears verbatim in the Phase Loop table and again in Decomposition Design. The anti-pattern table pays the same meaning a third time.
refuted_findings.proposed_fix: Drop anti-pattern rows that merely negate a rule already stated positively elsewhere; keep only genuinely new failure modes (e.g. "Skip Phase 3 because tests exist", "Silently delete dead code") that aren't restated as positive rules elsewhere in the document.
refuted_findings.reason: panel 1/3 confirmed | REFUTED — the quoted row appears verbatim, but it adds rationale ("kills git blame and reviewability") not present in the positive statements ("one-move-per-commit" in Phase Loop/Decomposition Design), so it isn't merely the same meaning restated negated; it's reinforcing the rule with a distinct reason, which doesn't clearly fit the cited "duplication" pattern. || REFUTED — the quoted anti-pattern row adds a concrete failure mode (combining extract+rename+reformat) and a specific consequence (breaks git blame) not present in the positive "one mechanical move per commit" statements, so it isn't a pure negated restatement of the same meaning. || CONFIRMED — the quoted anti-pattern row appears verbatim in the table, and it does restate a rule already stated positively in "Decomposition Design": "one mechanical move per commit (`git mv`-friendly, blame-preserving)" — the same phrase and same git-blame justification recur in both places.

refuted_findings.rule: Single source of truth / Duplication [craft] (Pruning and drift) — keep each meaning in one authoritative place so changing the behaviour is a one-place edit; duplication inflates a meaning's rank on the ladder past its real importance.

AND zero unresolved hypotheses (DEFERRED requires written rationale plus `Deferred reviewed: yes`).
